key_insight: EG-VQA shifts VideoQA evaluation beyond just whether an answer is correct and asks whether the answer is actually supported by relevant video evidence. It introduces a benchmark for checking grounded, temporally localized reasoning in Video-LLMs.
problem_solved: Existing VideoQA benchmarks mainly score final answer accuracy, which can hide models that guess correctly without using the right evidence. This paper addresses the lack of evaluation for evidence grounding and temporal support in video question answering.
method: Construct an open-ended benchmark, EG-VQA, focused on evidence-grounded video question answering.
Evaluate whether model predictions are supported by relevant temporal segments in the video, not just whether the final answer matches.
Benchmark Video-LLMs on both answer quality and grounding quality to expose mismatches between prediction and evidence use.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more realistic way to measure whether video models truly understand what they see. It helps identify models that are accurate by chance and supports development of more trustworthy, explainable VideoQA systems.

paper_title: EG-VQA: Benchmarking Verifiable Video Question Answering with Grounded Temporal Evidence
paper_authors: Linpeng Huang, Weixing Chen, Zexin Chen, Yang Liu, Liang Lin
